title: Capstone
tagline: Assemble everything you built into one shareable AI PM portfolio piece.

concept.intro: Nothing new to learn this week — just assembly. You've built a scorecard, a prompt template, a guardrail file, a prototype brief, and a review rubric, all for the same fictional feature. That's not a coincidence: it's meant to read as one coherent piece of AI PM work when you put it side by side.

sections.heading: Why this is worth showing your manager
sections.body: Five separate exercises don't obviously add up to anything. One document that walks a single feature — Northwind's Returns Assistant — from idea, through spec, through guardrails, through prototype, through review rubric, reads as exactly what an AI PM does day to day. That's the point of exporting it.

sections.heading: What to do with this on real work
sections.body: Each section below is a template you've now used once. The fastest way to make this stick is to run the same five steps on one real (non-sensitive, or fully within Gemini) feature idea in the next two weeks, before the habit fades.

scenario.context: This section pulls together what you built in Weeks 1 through 5, automatically, from what's saved in your browser.
scenario.brief: Add a short closing reflection, then export the full portfolio piece as one Markdown file.

exercise.instructions: Write a short reflection, then export. If any earlier week is incomplete, finish it first — the export pulls in whatever you've saved so far.

prompts.label: Closing reflection
prompts.help: In a few sentences: what's the one habit from these five weeks you're most likely to actually use on real work next month?
prompts.placeholder: e.g. Writing the guardrail file before handing anything to an agent — I've been skipping straight from idea to ticket, and this gives engineering something concrete to build against.
